title: Freya's Missing Pie Mystery
markdown:
The sun popped over the trees, painting the sky in brilliant stripes of pink and gold. A truly spectacular start. Freya the falcon blinked her bright, sharp eyes. Today felt different. A fizzy-buzzy feeling tickled her talons. It was a perfect day for pie. A magnificent, melt-in-your-beak kind of pie.

She zipped from her cozy nest, a blur of brown feathers. Down, down, down to the windowsill. Where her most marvellous, most scrumptious berry pie usually sat cooling. A perfect round of ruby red deliciousness. But the pie plate was bare. Not even a single crumb.

“Oh, nuts and twigs!” Freya squawked, a tremor rippling through her wings. Her heart did a frantic drum solo. Her tummy did a giant flip-flop. Her favourite pie, gone. Vanished.

Just then, a little rumble echoed from the bushes below. Biscuit the bear cub, all soft brown fur and a curious snout, popped his head out, his ears twitching. “Freya? What’s all the commotion? Did a giant sneeze just happen?”

“Biscuit! Disaster! Catastrophe! My pie! It’s vanished!” Freya fluttered, darting in tight circles. “Poof! Gone! Like magic, but not the fun kind!”

Biscuit ambled over, his big brown eyes wide. He carefully sniffed the air, his nose twitching like a detective’s antenna. “A missing pie? That sounds like an investigation!” He wiggled his nose with purpose. “I smell berries, a little bit. Faint, but definitely berries! This way!”

The grand adventure began. Freya zoomed ahead, a tiny whirlwind of determination, her keen eyes scanning every leaf and twig. Biscuit lumbered along behind, his big paws padding softly on the mossy ground, diligently following a faint trail of dark berry smudges that dotted the path like tiny fallen stars. Drip, drip, drip went the dew on the leaves. Tweet-tweet-tweet sang the busy birds. The woods buzzed with morning energy.

“Look!” Biscuit rumbled, pointing a big, gentle paw. “More marks! They’re getting thicker! And do you hear that?”

Freya tilted her head, her sharp falcon ears twitching. A faint, happy humming, like a lullaby sung by bumblebees, drifted from deeper in the trees. And the smell. Oh, the glorious smell. Sweet berries, warm honey, and something else, something deliciously earthy and comforting. It was an aroma that made Biscuit’s tummy give a hopeful rumble.

They tiptoed, tiptoed, tiptoed over a mossy log, careful not to disturb even a single sleeping ladybug. Then they peered into a sun-dappled clearing, where golden shafts of light danced through the leaves. And there, in the very middle, was a sight that made Freya’s beak drop open. A table. A wonderful table made of sturdy fallen logs, draped with the softest moss and decorated with bright cheerful wildflowers. And on it, a magnificent spread: glistening honeycombs dripping with amber goo, bowls piled high with plump wild strawberries, and a rather familiar-looking berry pie, now with a little nibble missing from its edge.

And presiding over this delightful feast, looking utterly content, was a small bear cub, with big bashful eyes and paws dusted with a fine layer of flour. It was Iorwen. Iorwen the shy bear cub from the Whispering Pines, the one who always hid behind his mother’s skirts.

“Iorwen?” Freya chirped, her voice a surprising mix of surprise and a touch of hurt. “You took my pie!”

Iorwen jumped, startled, his fluffy ears drooping low. “Oh! Oh dear. I did. But I was going to bring it back! Eventually! Honest!” He wrung his little paws together, looking incredibly anxious. “It’s for the Great Secret Feast!”

Freya tilted her head, her bright eyes questioning. “Great Secret Feast? What are you talking about, Iorwen?”

Iorwen took a deep, shaky breath. “Well, you see,” he began, his voice soft, “so many of the little creatures in the woods are shy. Like Pip the field mouse, and Flicker the baby owl. They don’t like big crowds, and they get terribly nervous. So I decided to host a secret feast, just for them. A place where they can giggle and munch and share stories without feeling watched by anyone.” He gestured to the beautifully set clearing. “But I’m not very good at gathering things, and some of my friends are even shyer than me. So I borrowed your pie. Just a little bit. To make it extra special!”

Freya looked at the colourful spread, the tiny cups made of acorn tops, the carefully arranged berries that looked like jewels. She saw Iorwen’s earnest, anxious face, his kind intention shining through. She could have huffed and puffed and demanded every crumb back. But seeing Iorwen’s shy, hopeful face felt wrong.

Biscuit nudged her gently with his big, soft shoulder. “He’s being kind, Freya. Even if he borrowed your pie. It’s a very thoughtful idea.”

Freya looked at the pie again. Yes, it was her pie, her absolute favourite. But Iorwen wasn’t being mean; he was being incredibly thoughtful and generous. It was a tough choice. She could insist on getting her pie back. Or she could see the wonderful thing he was doing.

“A secret feast for shy friends?” Freya brightened, a new brilliant idea sparking in her quick mind. “That’s a brilliant plan, Iorwen! But it needs more sparkle! More pizzazz! It needs flair!” She swooped down gracefully, landing beside the table with a soft flutter of wings. “I can help! I’m excellent at spotting shiny things, and I know just where to find the prettiest dewdrop diamonds! And maybe I have a few extra sunberries that could join the party!”

Iorwen’s shy smile grew, pushing away the worry lines. “Really?” he whispered, his eyes wide with hope.

“Really!” Freya declared with absolute certainty. She darted off like a shooting star, returning with delicate dew-kissed spiderwebs to drape like fairy lights and a small pile of precious plump sunberries she’d saved for a special occasion. Biscuit, with his mighty strength, helped arrange the flowers, carefully placing them in empty snail shells. Together, they transformed the clearing into a dazzling secret hideaway, a perfect spot for shy creatures.

Soon, tiny rustles and whispers began to fill the air. Pip the field mouse peeked from behind a bright red toadstool, his whiskers twitching nervously. Then Flicker the baby owl blinked from a low branch, his big eyes curious. One by one, the shy creatures arrived, their little faces filled with wonder and a touch of apprehension. They nibbled on the delicious food, they chatted in hushed tones, and they shared the wonderful feast Iorwen had planned. Iorwen beamed, his shyness replaced by a happy pride.

Freya even shared her extra sunberries, and Pip the field mouse squeaked a happy, grateful thank you.

As the sun climbed higher in the sky, casting long golden shafts through the trees, the last of the shy guests scampered and flapped away, their little faces full of happiness.

Freya and Biscuit stood beside Iorwen, watching them go. “That was amazing!” Freya chirped.

Iorwen gave a happy sigh, a contented rumble in his chest. “Thank you, Freya. Thank you, Biscuit. You made it even more special.”

“Anytime, pal!” Biscuit rumbled, patting Iorwen’s back gently, nearly sending the little cub tumbling.

Freya ruffled her feathers, a proud glint in her bright eyes. “My pie was super good, Iorwen. But helping you host this feast? That was even better!” She winked playfully. “And don’t worry, I think I have enough berries left back home for another pie later! Maybe we can make it together next time!”

With a shared grin, Freya and Biscuit turned towards home, their hearts light. Freya zipped ahead, a blur of brown feathers, already tasting the next pie in her mind, and the next morning, and the next fizzy-buzzy tickle in her talons.
